statement.text:
Let R be a commutative Noetherian ring with 1, and Λ an R-algebra, which is
finitely generated as R-module. Put T = {U ∈ Mod Λ | ∃ an exact Λ-sequence 0 →
P → Λ(n) → U → 0 for some n, with Pm ∼
                                                  (n)
                                             = Λm for every maximal ideal m of R}.
Denote by G(T ) the Grothendieck group of T relative to short exact sequences.
     a) Describe G(T ), in particular, what does it mean: [U ] = [V ] in G(T )?
    b) Conjecture: if dim(max(R)) = d < ∞, and there are two epimorphisms φ :
Λ(n) → U , ψ : Λ(n) → V , n > d, and [U ] = [V ] in G(T ), then Ker φ = Ker ψ.
                                                                     K. W. Roggenkamp
